items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline says what to do (keep September) and why (both candidates cost 27–28% more and stay in character less often). The decision block gives the price ($1.89 per 1,000 replies), why each candidate loses, and the main risks in watch: September holds character in only 65.8% of off-lane replies, the earlier qwen3.8-flash cost finding fails against this control, and 1017's reasoning share is lower. The flag puts the late criteria on screen. A small weakness: c1, the first claim, is the character reading, while cost (c2) actually decides the call.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 (pass rate within the 15-point margin) leads to c2 (cost decides), then c3 (corrected in-character drops) and c4/c5 (where the loss sits). The explore row agrees with decision_sensitivity, which holds at every margin with flip margins 10.8 and 5.8. options_dominance confirms September dominates both candidates. There are small seams. The lede calls qwen3.8-flash's 7.6-point pass-rate drop 'worse in character', though Method defines pass rate and in-character rate as separate figures (the in-character drop is 6.0). Method also says token counts were not reported, yet watch cites reasoning shares of output (55% vs 76%).

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: September's weak axis is visible (watch: 65.8% in character off-lane), and the intervals are read correctly in c1 and c3. Two framings are stronger than the data. First, the headline and c3 say 1017 stays in character less often, but that rests on one of four character readings: its pass rate (-3.0, -7.4 to +1.3), graded outcome (+0.014, adjusted p=1) and transcript score (+0.017, adjusted p=1) are all unseparated. Only persona.holds_character is separated (-4.7, -8.2 to -1.3). The omitted entry hides this by saying the outcome and transcript scores 'restate the in-character finding', which is true for qwen3.8-flash only. Second, watch says the earlier qwen3.8-flash cost finding is 'contradicted here', but next[0] admits it may have used a different control. Against another baseline it would not be a contradiction.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing omitted changes the call. Booth-offstage, delivery and failed-reply notices are all unseparated in contrasts_list. The p95 cost tails are higher for both candidates ($6.20 and $8.27 vs $5.30 per 1,000), so they only strengthen the call. Strata beyond the top four are 17 cases or fewer, mostly 10 or under. The margin does not move the call at any value. The misstated reason on the outcome/transcript omission is scored under item 3 because it does not change the decision.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The snapshot's confounds are handled. The reasoning ratio is carried into watch and next[4]. confound:model is fine: levers_effects shows the model is the only and isolated setting. The judge and simulator caveats go to next[2] and next[3]. But cost decides the call, and it is averaged over different trial sets: 864 of 897 trials for September, 828 of 895 for qwen3.8-flash and 879 of 897 for 1017, covering 294, 285 and 295 cases. Method prints these n's without saying the gap cannot matter. It cannot: even if qwen3.8-flash's 67 missing trials cost nothing, its mean would be about $2.25 per 1,000, still above $1.89. The report should show that.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: All five name an experiment or check and what it settles: reconcile the prior cost finding's control and prices, rewrite the off-lane directive and re-run on September, calibrate the judge, record the simulator settings, and match 1017's reasoning share. One is missing: the flag says the aspect, control, margin and floor were all set after the results, yet no next step declares them before the next round.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The c1 forest with its margin line and the c3 corrected forest fit their claims, and c4's unpaired strata bars are labelled as leads. c2 shows per-arm means over unequal trial sets. The paired, corrected cost contrasts (+$0.000616 per reply for qwen3.8-flash, +$0.000174 to +$0.000853; +$0.000492 for 1017, +$0.000174 to +$0.000811) would show 'costs more' directly. c5's block does not support its sentence: of the four cards, only T67 brushes off and then answers. T15 fails on a spoken line, T70 answers directly with no brush-off, and T44's reason names no brush-off. The block also shows candidates only, but September's kept off-lane failures (T14, T42, T64) fail the same way. So the block cannot tell the candidates apart from the control.

findings.finding: The claim says the kept failures brush off a non-music ask and then answer it, but only one of the four cards shown clearly does (T67). T15 fails on a queued spoken line (the caption admits it), T70 (qwen3.8-flash) answers 'cold wash, 30 max, inside out' with no brush-off, and T44's judge reason names advice but no brush-off. Restate it as 'the persona answers the non-music ask, sometimes after a brush-off'. Also add, or name, September's kept off-lane failures (T14, T42, T64), which fail the same way. That supports next[1] (a directive fix, not a model change).

Omitted: 'the judge's ordinal outcome and transcript scores ... restate the in-character finding' is true for qwen3.8-flash (-0.21 and -0.13, separated) but false for 1017 (+0.014 and +0.017, adjusted p=1). Say that 1017's gap shows on the in-character rate alone, and soften the headline and c3 wording for 1017 to match.

Cost decides the call, but the bars compare per-arm means over unequal trial sets (864, 828 and 879 trials; 294, 285 and 295 cases). Use or add the paired, Holm-corrected cost contrasts: qwen3.8-flash +$0.000616 per reply (+$0.000379 to +$0.000853), 1017 +$0.000492 (+$0.000174 to +$0.000811). Also state that the unreported costs cannot reverse the call: even if they were zero, qwen3.8-flash would be about $2.25 per 1,000.

The lede says qwen3.8-flash is 'worse in character, down 7.6 points', but 7.6 is the pass-rate drop. Method defines the in-character rate as a separate figure (its corrected drop is 6.0). Name the figure the lede quotes.

Watch says the earlier finding that qwen3.8-flash lowers production cost is 'contradicted here', while next[0] allows that it used a different control. Say it does not hold against September in this run, not that it is contradicted.

Method says token counts were not reported, so cost cannot be split into price and length. Yet watch cites reasoning shares of output (55% vs 76%). Say where the reasoning share comes from, or a reader will take the two as contradictory.

No next step declares the aspect, control, margin and floor before the next round, though the flag says all four were set after the results. Add that declaration and what it settles: a pre-registered call.
Explore: '{arm:1017} below {aspects.character adherence (v2).flip_margin.1017}.' prints '5.8.' with no unit. Add 'points' as on the qwen3.8-flash clause.

invariant_concerns: All 36 figure keys read through figure_keys_check, and all 10 report-reach caveats appear in confidence. The two short_run caveat ids carry run UUIDs (short_run:01a170ab-..., short_run:01a17121-...). If the page renders caveat ids above the appendix, invariant 5 fails; the caveat text itself names no id.
